name: Congenital Dyserythropoietic Anemia Type V

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Congenital Dyserythropoietic Anemia Type V

criteria.description: Presence of multinuclear erythroblasts in bone marrow aspirate
Severe anemia with reticulocytopenia and ineffective erythropoiesis
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the KLF1 gene
Bone marrow erythroid hyperplasia with dyserythropoietic features
Exclusion of other types of congenital dyserythropoietic anemia by genetic and morphological studies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multinuclear erythroblasts, severe anemia, and confirmed KLF1 gene mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, hematological, morphological, and genetic findings.

searchTerms: red blood cells with multiple nuclei
immature red cells with several nuclei
bone marrow cells with many nuclei
severe low red blood cell count
serious anemia with few young red cells
pale skin from low red blood cells
skin looks lighter due to anemia
yellowing of skin from red cell breakdown
skin and eye yellowing due to destroyed red cells

occasional.notes: Less pronounced than in other CDA types
Due to chronic transfusions or ineffective erythropoiesis

searchTerms: cardiac issues due to low red cells

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms related to severe anemia
searchTerms: brain problems due to low blood

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to iron overload
searchTerms: endocrine issues due to excess iron
gland dysfunction caused by iron overload

laboratory: Severe anemia with low reticulocyte count
Bone marrow aspirate showing multinuclear erythroblasts and erythroid hyperplasia
imaging: Splenomegaly and hepatomegaly on abdominal ultrasound
Skeletal X-rays may show mild abnormalities
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in KLF1 gene confirmed by molecular genetic testing
other: Exclusion of other CDA types by genetic and morphological criteria

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of internuclear chromatin bridges in erythroblasts
Less frequent multinuclear erythroblasts compared to Type V
Mutations in erythrocyte membrane protein genes

redFlags: Severe transfusion-dependent anemia in infancy or early childhood
Presence of multinuclear erythroblasts on bone marrow examination
